## Statement

**Lyapunov's inequality** says that the $L^r$ norms of a random variable are
increasing in $r$. It is a special case of the [[holder-inequality]], and
explains why higher-order [[convergence-in-lp-norm|$L^s$ convergence]] implies
lower-order $L^r$ convergence.

:::{.theorem data-title="Lyapunov's Inequality"}

For a random variable $X$ and $0 < r < s < \infty$,
$$
(\mathbb{E}[\lvert X \rvert^r] )^{1/r}\leq  (\mathbb{E}[\lvert X \rvert ^s])^{1/s}.
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

Hölder's inequality states that for $p,q>1$ with $1/p+1/q=1$
$$
|\mathbb{E}[UV]|\leq \mathbb{E}|UV|\leq (\mathbb{E}|U|^p)^{1/p}\cdot (\mathbb{E}|V|^q)^{1/q}.
$$
Take $U=\lvert X \rvert^r$, $V=1$ and $p=s/r>1$. Then
$$
\mathbb{E}\lvert X \rvert ^r\leq (\mathbb{E}\lvert X \rvert ^{rp})^{1/p} = (\mathbb{E}\lvert X \rvert^s )^{r/s},
$$
and raising both sides to the power $1/r$ gives the result.

:::
